diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

null_resource.update_kubeconfig has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but the dependency is already established implicitly: the provisioner command references module.eks.cluster_name (and module.eks is listed in implicit_deps). The explicit depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.delete_daemonset has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but this is already established transitively through its dependency on null_resource.update_kubeconfig, which itself depends on module.eks.

helm_release.karpenter has an explicit depends_on on data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster, but the dependency is already established transitively: helm_release.karpenter depends on module.karpenter, whose depends_on already includes data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster.

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but module.eks is already an implicit dependency via its triggers (module.eks.cluster_primary_security_group_id / cluster_security_group_id).
null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class has an explicit depends_on on module.karpenter, but module.karpenter is already an implicit dependency via its triggers (module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn).

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class has an explicit depends_on on null_resource.update_kubeconfig, but the dependency is already established transitively via helm_release.karpenter, which depends on null_resource.update_kubeconfig.

null_resource.apply_node_pool has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but this is already established transitively through its dependency on null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class, which depends on module.eks.

null_resource.apply_node_pool has an explicit depends_on on helm_release.karpenter, but this is already established transitively through its dependency on null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class, which depends on helm_release.karpenter.

null_resource.apply_node_pool has an explicit depends_on on null_resource.update_kubeconfig, but this is already established transitively through its dependency on null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class (and helm_release.karpenter), which both depend on null_resource.update_kubeconfig.

null_resource.delete_daemonset runs `kubectl delete daemonset aws-node`, removing the AWS VPC CNI from the cluster. This must only happen after Calico is installed and able to take over pod networking — i.e. after the Tigera operator is applied and the Calico Installation resource is created. Currently it only depends on null_resource.update_kubeconfig (and module.eks), which guarantees cluster reachability but not that Calico is in place; deleting aws-node too early can leave nodes without pod networking.
